newsitem.title: GHANA: Ghana plans $365 million development at ports.
newsitem.headline: Ghana plans $365 million development at ports.

text.p: Ghana's Takoradi and Tema ports are to be refurbished and modernised in a $365 million development plan, an official of the Ghana Ports and Harbours Authority (GPHA) told Reuters.
The authority expects increased traffic due to last year's creation of Free Trade Zones around Ghana's ports and hopes the development plan will start in earnest early in 1998.
"We have drawn up a 15-year master plan to recondition our ports in order to meet current trends in the maritime industry," said Paul Asare Ansah, a senior GPHA spokesman said.

With a total of 6.7 million tonnes handled in 1996, the two ports were working well below their total capacity of 15 million tonnes a year. However, water depths are insufficient for the newest container ships, while certain equipment is lacking.

"We are going to build new container terminals, which will be fitted with gantry cranes. The port of Tema will be dredged from the current depth of 9.6 metres to a depth of 14 metres, to enable very large container vessels to enter. Additional berths for the handling of liquid and dry bulk cargo, including cocoa and Liquefied Petroleum Gas, will be built," said Asare Ansah.
"We are soliciting for funds for these projects. Government is committed to increase privatisation of certain port services in order to attract private funds," he added.
In 1996 Ghana's ports acquired new equipment including tugboats and mobile crane.
Last year 1,127 vessels called at Tema port, compared with 993 in 1995, according to official figures.
Cargo throughput at Tema was 4.2 million tonnes of imports (3.9 million in 1995) and 690,000 tonnes of exports (681,000 in 1995).
Turnaround time (average hours spent in port) at Tema was 53.4 as against 57.7 in 1995.
At Takoradi a total of 500 vessels called in 1996, as against 407 the previous year.
Cargo throughput at Takoradi was 755,000 tonnes of imports (657,000 in 1995) and 1.04 million tonnes of exports (1.2 million in 1995).
Modernisation already started at Takoradi port resulted in a sharp fall in turnaround time last year to 40.1 hours from 65.4 in 1995 and 95.6 in 1994, officials said.
